problem: Find $(3a+b)\cdot c+(2b-2c)\cdot d,$ if $c\cdot a=3,$ $c\cdot b=-2,$ $b\cdot d=-1,$ and $d\cdot c=2.$

feedback.problem: Find $(3a-4b)\cdot c+(2b)\cdot d,$ if $c\cdot a=-2,$ $c\cdot b=4,$ and $d\cdot b=5.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the fact that the dot product is linear in the first variable, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3a-4b)\cdot c+(2b)\cdot d & =(3a)\cdot c-(4b)\cdot c+(2b)\cdot d \\  & =3(a\cdot c)-4(b\cdot c)+2(b\cdot d).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we can use the fact that the dot product is symmetric to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(a\cdot c)-4(b\cdot c)+2(b\cdot d) & =3(c\cdot a)-4(c\cdot b)+2(d\cdot b).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for $c\cdot a,$ $c\cdot b$ and $d\cdot b,$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}3(c\cdot a)-4(c\cdot b)+2(d\cdot b) & =3(-2)-4(4)+2(5) \\  & =-6-16+10 \\  & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $(3a-4b)\cdot c+(2d)\cdot b=-12.$
